# Keys you hand over - qa-failure-analyst

## Outputs

- `work/triage.json` - a verdict with evidence is the analyst's; s7_pretriage.py writes only the rows marked `source: code` (a manual check whose own record says what stopped it), never over an analyst row; s7_reorder.py finish writes only `carried_attempts` and `carried_by: s7_reorder` on the row that asked for a `reorder`, after the edit was a pure move and the repair run stayed red; s7_reorder.py mark_fixed (the `mark-fixed` mode) writes only `fix_result: fixed` on such a carried row, once the critic approved
  Keys the validator requires: `triage`.
- `work/bug-drafts/` - a draft is not a bug; the reporter files it after gate B
- `work/place-answers/` - your scratch for an answer, one file per place, passed to `place_answers.py write --file`; keys: `place`, `answer` (bug|not_a_bug|requirement_silent|impossible), `expectation` {`source` (requirement|question|person|none; not none for a bug), `id`, `quote`}, `seen` {`quote`, `capture`}, `question` (requirement_silent), `why` (impossible, not_a_bug), `draft` (bug), `walk` (optional)

Required at your stop (stage S7): `work/triage.json`.

## Witness

Your witness artifact (stages.json `witness`): `work/triage.json`.

## Handoff form

Contract `s7-analyst-to-automator` (fill `work/handoffs/<dispatch>.yaml`; `handoff_check.py` reads it):

- `inputs_read[].version` (required) - the report the triage was taken from
- `inputs_read[].failures` (required) - how many rows were triaged
- `header.window` (required) - the instance ids handed for repair
- `header.verdict` (required) - one of vocabulary.header_verdicts
- `scope[].id` (required) - instance id
- `scope[].state` (required) - TEST_BUG|TEST_BUG:collection|FLAKY|reorder
- `scope[].reason` (required) - a verdict of at most 80 characters - the explanation lives in the artifact
- `scope[].case` (required) - case id
- `scope[].round` (required) - r of 2
- `repairs[].id` (required) - instance id
- `repairs[].kind` (required) - repair|reorder
- `repairs[].verdict` (required) - TEST_BUG|TEST_BUG:collection|FLAKY|APP_BUG
- `repairs[].evidence` (required) - path of the log or artifact the verdict rests on
- `repairs[].problem` (required) - what the test does wrong, one sentence - about the test, never about the product
- `repairs[].expected` (required) - what the test should do instead, concretely - the assertion, the fixture, the wait condition, the selector
- `repairs[].fix` (required) - what to change, one sentence
- `repairs[].check` (required) - the command that shows the author it is satisfied - normally the repair_verify run
- `repairs[].mechanism` (required) - one of vocabulary.flaky_mechanisms - isolation|race|timing|shared_state|teardown|environment|unknown
- `repairs[].rerun_series` (required) - path of the three isolated reruns that proved the flakiness
- `repairs[].then_lines` (required) - the Then lines as they stand now - they must read the same after the fix
- `not_for_repair[].id` (required) - instance id
- `not_for_repair[].verdict` (required) - APP_BUG|ENV_ISSUE|APP_CHANGED|CASE_DEFECT|ASSERT_STRICTER|NOT_EXECUTED|RUNNER_MISREAD_EVIDENCE|NO_DEFECT
- `not_for_repair[].where_it_went` (required) - bug draft path | the stage that owns it | the rework dispatch | "Left with you" for ASSERT_STRICTER - the person decides | "the runner judges it again" for RUNNER_MISREAD_EVIDENCE - the driver sends the check back to S6
- `claims.every_repair_names_evidence_expected_and_check` (required) - true|false
- `claims.no_app_bug_expectation_was_handed_for_repair` (required) - true|false
- `claims.every_flaky_verdict_carries_three_isolated_reruns_and_a_mechanism` (required) - true|false
- `unresolved[].id` (required) - instance id
- `unresolved[].reason` (required) - one of vocabulary.unresolved_reasons
- `unresolved[].detail` (required) - what exactly is missing, and what would settle it
- `blocked.field` (only when blocked) - the field of this file the role cannot fill
- `blocked.problem` (only when blocked) - what the role tried and what refused it, verbatim
- `blocked.tried[]` (only when blocked) - command or step, and its answer
- `blocked.data[]` (only when blocked) - path of anything the conductor needs to see

Every handoff form shares one skeleton (`common_shape` of handoffs/index.yaml): `inputs`, `inputs_read`, `header`, `scope`, `artifacts`, `claims`, `unresolved`, `blocked`.
